items.followUp: Define a hypothesis and state how it differs from a theory.

rubric.why: A theory is an explanation supported by extensive testing and evidence.
rubric.description: Defines a theory as a well-tested explanation of natural phenomena.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a theory is a well-tested explanation.

rubric.why: A law describes a regularity observed in nature rather than explaining it.
rubric.description: Defines a law as a statement describing a consistent pattern or phenomenon in nature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a law describes a regular pattern or phenomenon in nature.

modelAnswer: A theory is a well-tested explanation of natural phenomena, supported by repeated investigations and evidence.
A law is a statement that describes a consistent pattern or phenomenon in nature.

items.followUp: State two ways classification helps biologists study organisms.

rubric.why: Grouping organisms makes their diversity more manageable to study.
rubric.description: States that classification organizes organisms into groups and makes them easier to study.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that classification makes the study of organisms easier.

rubric.why: Classification supports identification and helps reveal relationships among organisms.
rubric.description: States that classification helps identify organisms or understand their relationships.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning identification or relationships among organisms.

modelAnswer: Classification organizes the great variety of organisms into groups and makes them easier to study.
It helps identify organisms and understand relationships among them.

items.followUp: How did Robert Hooke's observation of cork contribute to cell biology?

rubric.why: The year and specimen identify Hooke's historical observation.
rubric.description: States that Hooke examined cork in 1665.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning both 1665 and cork.

rubric.why: Hooke observed compartments in cork and gave them the name cells.
rubric.description: Describes the small compartments he observed and states that he named them cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the compartments and their name.

modelAnswer: In 1665, Robert Hooke examined a thin slice of cork under a microscope.
He observed many small, box-like compartments and named them cells.

items.followUp: State two functions of the endoplasmic reticulum.

rubric.why: The Golgi apparatus processes materials received from the endoplasmic reticulum.
rubric.description: States that the Golgi apparatus modifies proteins or lipids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning modification of proteins or lipids.

rubric.why: Packaging materials into vesicles enables their transport or secretion.
rubric.description: States that the Golgi apparatus packages materials into vesicles for transport or secretion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it packages materials into vesicles for transport or secretion.

modelAnswer: The Golgi apparatus modifies and sorts proteins and lipids received from the endoplasmic reticulum.
It packages them into vesicles for transport or secretion from the cell.
